title: mdatron verify --json output envelope
description: The machine interface of `mdatron verify --json`. Versioned: mdatron_output_version tracks THIS schema (currently 3.0.0). A published contract (DESIGN.md § Diagnostics are a versioned contract) — consumers pin and validate against it.

mdatron_output_version.description: Semver of this envelope schema. Moves with the schema; a change here signals a contract change.

envelope_schema.description: The $id of the published schema this envelope was produced under, so a consumer can pin the exact contract without joining the version onto a URL template. An identifier, not a fetch target; the resolvable copy ships in the repo and via `mdatron schema`.

mdatron_version.description: The running mdatron crate version (distinct from the envelope version).

pipeline_status.description: Whether the verification pipeline ran to completion. "failed" means orchestration broke before a verdict (see pipeline_error) — distinct from a completed run that found errors.

pipeline_error.description: Present only when pipeline_status is "failed" (omitted on success). Carries the failure reason IN the envelope so a --json --quiet consumer receives it (the stderr note is suppressed by --quiet). `kind` disambiguates the senses the single MDATRON-E0080 code conflates.

code.description: The pipeline-failure namespace code, stable across kinds (MDATRON-E0080).

kind.description: The failure class, so a consumer can branch without parsing prose.

message.description: The rendered failure reason, project-root-relativized (no host-layout leak).

summary.description: Per-severity finding counts plus the count of files this run validated.

error_count.description: Number of error-severity findings (drives exit code 1).

warning_count.description: Number of warning-severity findings (exit 0 unless --deny-warnings escalates).

lint_count.description: Number of lint-severity findings (standing informational signals, e.g. governance-weakening records).

files_checked.description: the number of files this run VALIDATED (ran the per-file schema and rule checks on), not a count of files that produced findings; a clean run over N files reports N, an empty jurisdiction reports 0

families.description: Per-verify activity of the check families as a tri-state plus a reason: active = data supplied and the check ran this pass; inert = configured but did no work (e.g. scoped to no file); inactive = not configured. The reason makes the audit signal falsifiable. Forward-extensible (3.0.0, #145/#147): the named families below are always present; new families appear over time as additional members of the same shape, so a consumer must tolerate unknown family keys.

schema.description: Frontmatter JSON-Schema conformance per declared schema_class.

route.description: The route table: the closed-world allowlist over the governed tree.

pin.description: Content pins: sha256 attestations by governing documents over governed files.

vocabulary.description: The naming register: prose scanned against the supplied term/label/anti-pattern registry.

citation.description: file:line citation verification against the run snapshot.

marker.description: Marker-line references: declared-pattern lines resolving by name into a target document.

code_catalog.description: Adopter code-token resolution against declared code catalogs.

section.description: Section-structural count/disjointness assertions over body sections.

inputs.description: Governance-input lineage: each input this run consumed, mapped to a sha256 digest of the exact bytes it read. Keys are the governance files found and read (config.yaml, routes.yaml, vocabulary.yaml, pins.yaml, code-catalogs.yaml — each present only when loaded) plus one aggregate digest each for the schemas and patterns directories (sorted filenames + per-file content digests; omitted when the directory is absent or empty). Lets a consumer attest WHICH configuration produced a verdict and detect config drift between runs. Deterministic across platforms; always empty on a failed pipeline (partial lineage is deliberately not attested).

timings.description: Run-phase wall-clock timings in milliseconds. Present ONLY under `verify --timings`: timings are the envelope's sole non-deterministic zone, so the default envelope stays byte-identical across runs on an unchanged tree.

total_ms.description: Wall-clock of the whole verification run.

load_ms.description: Loading configuration inputs: config, schemas, patterns, routes, pins, vocabulary, code catalogs.

capture_ms.description: The governed walk plus the immutable snapshot build, through the capture-complete seam.

check_ms.description: The per-file loop and cross-file checks, through result ordering.

findings.description: The run's findings, sorted by root-relative file path then code (deterministic across platforms).

state.description: active = data supplied and the check ran; inert = configured but did no work this pass; inactive = not configured.

reason.description: Engine-authored explanation of the state, making the activity signal falsifiable.

code.description: The namespaced diagnostic code (MDATRON-Ennnn/Wnnnn/Lnnnn, or an adopter-defined code for DSL-rule findings).

severity.description: error gates (exit 1); warning reports (escalatable via --deny-warnings); lint is a standing informational signal.

summary.description: The short kebab-case headline (e.g. dead-link-target). For DSL-rule findings this is the adopter's rule id.

message.description: The engine-authored explanation. Adopter-derived values never ride inline here — they are carried in quoted[] (the marking discipline).

help.description: Engine-authored remediation guidance, or null when the message suffices.

explain_ref.description: The code to pass to `mdatron explain`, or null when no explain page resolves (e.g. adopter-defined codes).

location.description: Where the finding points: a project-root-relative, forward-slashed file path plus a 1-based line (0 = no location applicable) and column (0 = whole line).

file.description: Project-root-relative path with forward slashes — byte-identical across Unix and Windows (DEF4).

line.description: 1-based line; 0 means no location applies (e.g. a pipeline-level finding).

fingerprint.description: A line-churn-stable identity for cross-run trending: v1 = sha256 (truncated to 16 bytes) over the finding's code, root-relative forward-slashed path, summary, each identity-bearing quoted region's label and content in order — a region quoting platform-variant engine prose (e.g. an OS error message) is excluded, so the same defect fingerprints identically across platforms — and a 0-based occurrence ordinal that distinguishes otherwise-identical findings in one run. Line/column are deliberately excluded so the fingerprint survives document churn; removing the first of two identical findings transfers its identity to the survivor (the SARIF partialFingerprints tradeoff). A future algorithm change mints a v2 prefix.

quoted.description: Adopter-derived text carried out-of-line (absent when empty — the emitter never produces an empty array, and minItems pins that: an emitted `quoted: []` would be a shape regression). Each region is untrusted adopter content, marked as such so a consumer need not infer it from the presence of the field.

label.description: Engine-authored name for what the quoted content is (e.g. "found", "section").

content.description: The raw adopter-derived text, verbatim (JSON-escaped by serialization only).

origin.description: Provenance of the content. Always "adopter": quoted content is adopter-derived by construction.

trusted.description: Always false: adopter content must never be treated as engine-authored instruction. The machine-readable form of the TTY `> ` prefix marking.
